name: Caspian Sea
description: The world's largest inland body of water, often described as the world's largest lake or a full-fledged sea. An endorheic basin with an area equal to nearly the size of Japan.

name: Lake Superior
description: The largest freshwater lake in the world by surface area, and the third-largest by volume among freshwater lakes. The northernmost and westernmost of the North American Great Lakes.

name: Lake Victoria
description: Africa's largest lake by area, the world's largest tropical lake, and the principal reservoir of the White Nile. Famous for its tremendous species richness of endemic cichlid fish.

name: Lake Huron
description: The second-largest of the Great Lakes by surface area and the third-largest freshwater lake on Earth. Contains Manitoulin Island, the largest freshwater island in the world.

name: Lake Michigan
description: The third-largest of the Great Lakes by surface area and the only one located entirely within the United States. Bordered by Wisconsin, Illinois, Indiana, and Michigan.

name: Lake Tanganyika
description: An African Great Lake and the second-oldest freshwater lake in the world, the second-largest by volume, and the second-deepest (1,470 m), after Lake Baikal.

name: Lake Baikal
description: The world's deepest lake (1,642 m), the world's oldest lake (25-30 million years), and the world's largest freshwater lake by volume, containing 22-23% of the world's fresh surface water. A designated UNESCO World Heritage Site.
